_note: B-65. DeviceR3 PowerShell levers over the offline mock device state (fixtures/tenant/<client>/devices.json). All R3 except device.unlock (R2); retire and wipe are irreversible and never use pre-authorized containment. No caps are set here: the R3 default applies (B-42). Graph and Defender permission names in graph_scopes are UNVERIFIED (see levers/powershell/DeviceR3/SOURCES.md). Mock only; no real RMM, Intune or Defender is called.

levers.name: device.lock
levers.description: Lock one device of the client (screen lock; the data stays). Mock of an Intune remote lock. Two lead approvals, one device per approval.

device.description: RMM device uid of the one device this call changes (lower-case GUID)

upn.description: userPrincipalName of the device's assigned user; must match the device record

impact.L1: One person cannot use their device until it is unlocked; locking the wrong machine stops someone's work, and an unsaved document may be lost.
impact.L2: A lost or stolen laptop is shut quickly; a locked front-desk PC can stop patient or customer check-in until it is unlocked.
impact.L3: The fast first step for a lost device becomes two approved, verified, audited steps with the blast radius shown, instead of a phone call nobody records.
impact.L4: Containing a lost device in minutes limits breach risk at every client; the owner must match the device, so one office's device is never touched for another.

levers.name: device.unlock
levers.description: Clear the lock on one device of the client. The undo of device.lock. Mock of an Intune action.

device.description: RMM device uid of the one device this call changes (lower-case GUID)

upn.description: userPrincipalName of the device's assigned user; must match the device record

impact.L1: One person can use their device again; unlocking a device that is still missing gives a finder access to it.
impact.L2: The client gets a recovered or wrongly locked device back; a wrong unlock reopens a device that was locked on purpose.
impact.L3: Reversing a lock is a verified, approved and audited step, and it restores exactly the state the lock changed.
impact.L4: A safe undo makes people willing to lock first and ask later, which protects every client.

levers.name: device.isolate
levers.description: Isolate one device of the client from the network, keeping only the management service. Mock of a Defender for Endpoint machine isolation. Two lead approvals, one device per approval.

device.description: RMM device uid of the one device this call changes (lower-case GUID)

upn.description: userPrincipalName of the device's assigned user; must match the device record

impact.L1: One person cannot work online on this device until it is released; isolating the wrong machine halts their work.
impact.L2: A device that may carry malware stops spreading it; isolating a clinic's only front-desk PC stops patient check-in, so the dry-run says when a device is the only one for its role.
impact.L3: Containment becomes two approved, audited steps with the blast radius shown, and the release lever puts the network access back.
impact.L4: Fast containment limits ransomware at every client; one device per approval stops a mistake from isolating a whole office.

levers.name: device.release
levers.description: Release one device of the client from network isolation. The undo of device.isolate. Mock of a Defender for Endpoint action.

device.description: RMM device uid of the one device this call changes (lower-case GUID)

upn.description: userPrincipalName of the device's assigned user; must match the device record

impact.L1: One person gets their device back online; releasing a device that is still infected lets it reach the network again.
impact.L2: The client resumes work after an incident; a wrong release re-exposes the office to a device that was cut off on purpose.
impact.L3: Releasing is as controlled as isolating: two leads, a verified requester and an audit record, and it reverses isolate exactly.
impact.L4: A deliberate release step keeps a quick isolate from becoming a forgotten outage at any client.

levers.name: device.retire
levers.description: Retire one device of the client: company data and management are removed, the personal side stays. Irreversible. Mock of an Intune retire. Two lead approvals, one device per approval, approval under 24 hours old.

device.description: RMM device uid of the one device this call changes (lower-case GUID)

upn.description: userPrincipalName of the device's assigned user; must match the device record

impact.L1: One person loses company apps and data on this device for good; retiring the wrong device means lost work that only a backup can bring back.
impact.L2: A leaver's or lost device stops holding client data; a wrong retire removes data the practice may still need, and a device under legal hold is refused.
impact.L3: Offboarding hardware work becomes two approved, audited steps; the page says no undo so nobody approves it casually.
impact.L4: Company data leaves retired devices at every client without a person remembering to do it, and never from a device the owner does not match.

levers.name: device.wipe
levers.description: Record a full wipe request for one device of the client. Irreversible. A person starts the wipe in the console after approval; nothing here does. Mock of an Intune wipe. Two lead approvals, one device per approval, approval under 24 hours old.

device.description: RMM device uid of the one device this call changes (lower-case GUID)

upn.description: userPrincipalName of the device's assigned user; must match the device record

impact.L1: Everything on this device is erased for good, including anything the person never saved elsewhere; the wrong device means lost work that only a backup can restore.
impact.L2: A stolen device stops being a breach risk; a wipe before a legal hold or an investigation is known destroys evidence, so held devices are refused and the client contact confirms.
impact.L3: The riskiest endpoint action needs two leads, a verified requester, the client's contact and a fresh approval, and the audit shows who approved this exact device.
impact.L4: Nobody wipes the wrong device: one device per approval, owner must match, no bulk path, and a person starts the wipe.
